item.description:
Massachusetts currently holds “closed” primaries so Democrats and Republicans can choose their own nominees. Unenrolled voters must choose which party primary to participate in. The winner of each party primary advances to the general election. Q3 would replace that system with a single, "open" primary in which every voter chooses among all candidates; the top two advance to November, even if they belong to the same party. If approved, the change would take effect in 2028.

item.title: [Itrfoundation] Protecting Every Taxpayer in Red Oak
item.description:
Iowans for Tax Relief Foundation was in Red Oak this week to talk with southwest Iowans about Amendment One and answer questions about the taxpayer protection that will appear on the November 3 ballot.

Amendment One would require a two-thirds vote of both the Iowa House and Iowa Senate to increase individual or corporate income-tax rates or create a new state tax measured by income. It would not prohibit an income-tax increase, but it would require broader agreement among lawmakers before one could take effect.
